skills.name: brainstorm
skills.description: Think a new project through with the user before anything is built. Interview them for intent, research in the background, converge on a direction, and write the design. Use for "brainstorm", "let's brainstorm", "new project", or starting a product from scratch.
skills.forYou: find out what you actually want, with research, before any code exists.
skills.fixes: The agent guessed what I meant and built the wrong thing.

skills.name: grilling
skills.description: Stress-test a plan, decision or idea through rounds of pointed questions, each with a recommended answer. Use for "grill me", "poke holes in this", "challenge my plan", or when a design must converge on decisions.
skills.forYou: stress-test a plan in rounds of questions, each with a recommended answer.
skills.fixes: The agent acted on assumptions it never checked with me.

skills.name: research
skills.description: Investigate a defined question against primary sources and return a cited, dated answer. Use for "research X", "find out", docs or API facts, comparing options, or as a background lane for another skill; not for plain codebase explanation (explain-codebase).
skills.forYou: answer a question from primary sources, cited and dated.
skills.fixes: The agent answered from memory or a blog post and gave no source I could check.

skills.name: prototype
skills.description: Build a throwaway artifact to settle one uncertain design question. Use for "prototype", "spike", "mockup", "try a few versions", "does this state model feel right", or "what should this look like". Skip when the behavior is already settled.
skills.forYou: build a throwaway to answer one design question.
skills.fixes: A design question was argued in chat for an hour, or throwaway code ended up in production.

skills.name: writing-plans
skills.description: Turn an approved design or clear requirements into an implementation plan of small, independently testable tasks with exact files, interfaces and checks. Use for "write a plan", "plan this out", or before multi-step work.
skills.forYou: turn a design into small tasks with exact files, interfaces and tests.
skills.fixes: The plan grew into thousands of lines of code and took hours, and nothing got built.

skills.name: to-issues
skills.description: Break a design, plan or conversation into tracer-bullet issues with blocking edges, then publish them to GitHub Issues, Linear, or Markdown files (Obsidian-friendly). Use for "break this into issues", "create tickets", "make a backlog", "put this in Linear/GitHub".
skills.forYou: break work into tickets in GitHub, Linear or Markdown, each naming what blocks it.
skills.fixes: Work landed as one huge ticket, or as layers (all database, then all UI) that could not be tested alone.

skills.name: architecture-design
skills.description: Design or reshape a module, interface, seam, or subsystem before coding, or restructure existing code without changing behavior. Use for "design this", "architect", "refactor", "restructure", extract/move/rename/dedupe, or unclear ownership; skip routine edits that fit an established shape.
skills.forYou: design module boundaries, and refactor without changing behaviour.
skills.fixes: A refactor quietly changed behaviour, or a new design added layers that only passed arguments along.

skills.name: implement
skills.description: Execute an approved plan or set of issues to completion, task by task, with tests, verification and review. Use for "implement this", "build the plan", "work the issues", "start on ticket X".
skills.forYou: execute a plan or tickets to the end, yourself or with subagents.
skills.fixes: The agent stopped after every step to ask whether it should go on.

skills.name: working-style
skills.description: Proceed, then present: do reversible work, report why. Ask only about product direction, or before irreversible or outward-facing steps: force-push, shared merge, deleting data, publishing, messaging people.
skills.forYou: let the agent decide and do reversible work, and ask you only before steps it cannot undo.
skills.fixes: The agent stopped to ask "should I…?" about work it could have done and reported.

skills.name: orchestrate
skills.description: Run a long session as the coordinator of implementer and reviewer agents working tickets in parallel worktrees, under the user's standing orders. Use for "orchestrate", "run the factory", "work the backlog", "keep agents busy", or any session that dispatches many implementers.
skills.forYou: coordinate many implementer and reviewer agents under your standing orders.
skills.fixes: In long sessions I kept repeating the same reminders: keep agents busy, update the tracker, use this model.

skills.name: test-driven-development
skills.description: Build features and fix bugs test-first with red-green-refactor at agreed seams. Use for TDD, "write a failing test first", regression tests, or any behavior change with a testable seam.
skills.forYou: build each behaviour test-first: watch the test fail, then make it pass.
skills.fixes: The tests passed, but they would have passed even if the code were wrong.

skills.name: systematic-debugging
skills.description: Find the root cause of bugs, test failures, regressions, flaky or slow behavior before fixing. Use for "debug this", "diagnose", "why does X fail", anything broken, throwing, or slow, and before proposing any fix.
skills.forYou: reproduce, isolate and fix the root cause.
skills.fixes: The fix made the error go away but left the bug in place.

skills.name: frontend-design
skills.description: Design and build web UI that avoids template and AI-generated looks. Use when building or restyling pages, components, dashboards, or landing pages, when asked to "make it look good", and when UX flows, information architecture, or screen states need deciding first.
skills.forYou: design and check UI that doesn't look like a template.
skills.fixes: The interface the agent built looked like a generic template.

skills.name: verification-before-completion
skills.description: Gate any claim that work is done, fixed, passing, or ready on fresh evidence. Use right before saying "done", "fixed", or "passing", handing work back, committing, or opening a PR.
skills.forYou: prove a claim before saying "done".
skills.fixes: The agent said "done" when it meant "I think it's done".

skills.name: create-verification-skill
skills.description: Write a project's own verify-<app> skill that tells any agent how to launch the app from scratch, drive a feature like a user, capture evidence and clean up. Use for "make a verification skill", "how do agents prove changes work here", or when agents keep claiming done without running the app.
skills.forYou: write a project's verify skill so agents can prove changes in the real app.
skills.fixes: Agents had no scripted way to run the app, so "it works" was a guess.

skills.name: code-review
skills.description: Review a diff, branch, PR, or files for spec and standards fit, and trace what a change could break beyond the diff. Use for "review this", "what could this break", "blast radius", or when acting on review feedback.
skills.forYou: review a change and trace what it could break beyond its own diff.
skills.fixes: A change looked fine in its diff and broke something elsewhere.

skills.name: ci-pr-lifecycle
skills.description: Check or drive a branch, PR, and CI through to a finished state. Use for "is this ready", "CI status", "open a PR", "push and watch CI", "retry the failed job", or finishing a branch. Never merges without an explicit ask.
skills.forYou: drive a PR through CI to a finished state; it never merges unasked.
skills.fixes: Cleaning up after a merge, the agent deleted work that had never been committed.

skills.name: explain-codebase
skills.description: Explain how existing code works, and when asked why it is shaped that way. Use for "how does X work", walkthroughs, "where should this live", "why is this here", and design rationale. Read-only.
skills.forYou: explain how code works, and why it is shaped that way.
skills.fixes: The agent explained code from its names and folders, and gave guesses about intent as fact.

skills.name: wait-what
skills.description: Re-pitch your last message when it did not land. Use when the user is confused by your previous answer: "wait, what", "explain that normally", "I don't get it", "in plain English". One turn; no research.
skills.forYou: get the last answer again in plain words.
skills.fixes: The agent's answer was so dense with jargon that I couldn't follow it.

skills.name: handoff
skills.description: Write a handoff brief for another agent, session, or machine, or resume work from one. Use for "hand off", "write a handoff", "pick up where we left off", "take over from this brief or branch".
skills.forYou: write a handoff between sessions, or resume from one.
skills.fixes: A new session started cold and redid finished work, or trusted a stale summary.

skills.name: reflect
skills.description: Mine the current session for durable lessons and turn each into a concrete edit to a skill, an AGENTS.md, or an enforcement backlog item. Use for "reflect", "what did we learn", "update the skills from this session", or after a session full of corrections.
skills.forYou: turn a session's lessons into edits to skills, `AGENTS.md` or enforcement.
skills.fixes: The agent made the same mistake every session.

skills.name: technical-documentation
skills.description: Write or revise source-grounded docs: READMEs, tutorials, how-to guides, references, explanations, design docs, and user guides or SOPs for non-technical operators. Use when documentation must be accurate, scannable, and verified against the current system.
skills.forYou: write docs for developers or operators, checked against the real system.
skills.fixes: The docs described what the code used to do, or guessed at names and flags.

skills.name: unslop
skills.description: Remove AI tells from prose while keeping facts and voice. Use as the final pass on reports, docs, READMEs, proposals, PR descriptions, and posts, or when asked to humanize, tighten, or de-slop text. Skip code, logs, quotes, and short chat replies.
skills.forYou: strip AI tells from prose.
skills.fixes: The text read as if a model wrote it: filler openings, stock words, a triplet in every sentence.
